title: Basel III: international regulatory framework for banks
summary: BIS provides an index page to Basel III regulatory framework documents, including standards for capital requirements, market risk, liquidity coverage ratio, and net stable funding ratio. Basel III is an internationally agreed set of measures developed in response to the 2007-09 financial crisis to strengthen bank regulation, supervision, and risk management.
key_points: Basel III reforms have been integrated into the consolidated Basel Framework
Standards apply as minimum requirements to internationally active banks
Final post-crisis reforms endorsed by the Group of Governors and Heads of Supervision (GHOS) on December 7, 2017
Market risk framework adjustments endorsed by GHOS on January 14, 2019
Key components include: Minimum capital requirements for market risk, Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR), Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR)
Member jurisdictions committed to implementing standards within established timeframes
why_it_matters: Basel III sets the foundational regulatory capital and liquidity requirements for globally active banks. These standards affect bank balance sheets, risk-taking behavior, and ultimately credit availability and market liquidity. Understanding the regulatory framework is essential for assessing banking sector resilience and potential compliance costs.
market_structure_context: This page references the Basel III framework which directly governs bank capital requirements, risk-weighted assets, and market risk standards. Implementation phases extend from 2017 to 2028, affecting how banks structure their trading operations and maintain regulatory capital ratios.
